root.name: Dutch Defense: Blackmar's Second Gambit
root.moves: 1. d4 f5 2. e4 fxe4 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. f3

overview: The Staunton Gambit with 4.f3 instead of the main 4.Bg5. White offers a second pawn and wants to open the f-file and the centre with fxe4 or f3xe4. Black usually plays 4...exf3 5.Nxf3 e6 and has an extra pawn with a solid position, or 4...d5 5.fxe4 dxe4 and returns it. White gets open lines and a lead in development but Black can usually consolidate.

white_ideas.idea: Open the f-file and the centre with fxe4 or Nxf3 and develop quickly with Bc4 or Bg5.
Attack Black's king on the e8-h5 diagonal and the weak e6 square.

black_ideas.idea: Take on f3 and consolidate with ...e6 and ...Be7, keeping the extra pawn.
Play ...d5 and ...e5 to hit the centre and return material for the initiative.

typical_structures.structure: Open centre after e4 is taken, with White's f-pawn gone and Black pawns on e6, d5 or d6.

character.notes: White offers a second pawn for lines and tempo, so both sides take risks and tactics decide.

gambit.notes: After 2...fxe4 Black is a pawn up and 4...exf3 5.Nxf3 e6 keeps it, with White playing for development.

soundness.notes: Black can keep the extra material with careful play; the 4.f3 branch is considered dubious for White.

structure.notes: Open lines and pieces dominate after the pawns on e4 and f3 are exchanged.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom play 4.f3; chosen mainly for surprise.

level.notes: Needs knowledge of the forcing lines, but the gambit is dubious so never a beginner choice.

plan_phrases: open f-file and lead in development

sublines_that_differ.name: 4...d5 line
sublines_that_differ.how: Black returns a pawn for a calm position and White has an open f-file but no more than slight comfort.

character.reason: Pawns are being exchanged and the f-file and e8-h5 diagonal lead to concrete tactics.

gambit.reason: White is a pawn down after 2...fxe4 and the pawn can be kept.

soundness.reason: 4.f3 is less accurate than 4.Bg5 and Black can hold the extra pawn.

structure.reason: Central pawns are traded and play turns on open files and diagonals.

approach.reason: The 4.f3 sideline is seldom chosen by strong players.

level.reason: Dubious gambit so not beginner, but sidelines are short.

plans.reason: White plays for development and attack in return for the pawn.
